newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli CPI-linked bonds close lower.
newsitem.headline: Israeli CPI-linked bonds close lower.

text.p: Israeli CPI-linked bonds closed lower on Wednesday as investors remained on the sidelines waiting for the release of the February consumer price index on Friday, traders said.
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon -- issued for four years): +0.1 pct to 103.79
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.02 pct at 102.92
Volume was low at 143 million shekels.

"Investors are sitting on the fence waiting for the CPI release. Overall volume was very low and the market was quiet. CPI-linked bonds made a big move and now the market has reached a new equilibrium," said Danni Shamir at Israel Discount Bank.
Analysts predict the February consumer price index will show a 1.1-1.2 percent rise over January.

"Long CPI-linked bonds rose sharply during the last two weeks, rising for eight sessions in a row. Today's decline is only a technical correction before they resume their rise," said Michael Politzer at Central Securities Corp.
"Short-inflation linked bonds were mixed today as investors wait for the CPI. A higher than expected figure will lead to a further rise," Politzer added.
Shamir said unlinked bonds and Makams edged higher on a very low volume. "These bonds are less attractive now because they are more risky than CPI-linked bonds," he said.

Dollar-linked bonds closed higher after the shekel declined against the dollar. In the local market, the representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.3730 shekels against 3.3680 shekels on Tuesday.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
